item.title: Cabinet sets out AI plan, seeks partners beyond US and China
item.description:
Cabinet sets out AI plan, seeks partners beyond US and China

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The cabinet is establishing a vision of how to integrate AI into Dutch society so as to take advantage of its benefits, control reliance on foreign powers and strengthen national security.

Digital economy minister Willemijn Aerdts released 28-page vision letter to parliament on Friday, acknowledging that AI will “largely determine our future”.

“We want a Netherlands where AI makes everyone better and helps us move forward. Where a nurse has more time for patients, entrepreneurs can grow, and technology helps us with the major challenges of our time,” she said.

“That requires choices. Where do we want to lead the way and where do we draw the line? We don’t have to be able to do everything ourselves, but we do want to decide for ourselves which direction we take.”

The vision names Canada, Japan, Singapore and South Korea as “middle powers” the Netherlands wants to work with, alongside other EU member states.

It also says the Netherlands will keep working on “stable and predictable relations” with the US and China. The letter notes that the Netherlands has joined Pax Silica, a US-led partnership on chips, computing power and AI infrastructure.

The only funding figure in the vision is €120 million for Dutch participation in an EU-wide AI project, which was already set aside in September. The letter says more “targeted and structural investment” is needed in infrastructure, talent and research, but gives no amounts.

“This is a toothless tiger,” Volt leader Laurens Dassen told broadcaster NOS. “AI should be a top priority. It isn’t if there is no budget.”

Plans for computing power and datacentres, which use large amounts of electricity and water, will follow in the first quarter of 2027.

The cabinet is also exploring whether to set up a Dutch AI safety institute modelled on the UK’s AI Security Institute. An advisory report is due in December.

Aerdts and the education minister plan to agree a “media pact” with public and private media organisations, which will also cover how AI systems use journalistic content. No details on that have been given yet.

item.title: Activists occupy site of Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam
item.description:
Activists occupy site of Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Police are clearing a building site in Westpoort after pro-Palestinian activists occupied it this morning in protest to the city’s plans to build a massive data centre there, which will be leased to Microsoft.

Microsoft has acknowledged selling cloud and computing software to the Israeli military. The action was originally organised by the climate and justice group Geef Tegengas and joined by Extinction Rebellion and other groups. Other groups turned up and some stormed the site, and hung up Palestinian flags.

There was a confrontation between the police and activists this morning, according to broadcaster NOS, although the demonstration was allowed to continue after police surrounded them.

Some activists climbed onto cranes and the roof of the construction.

The €1 billion, 78MW campus is being built by Pure DC and is let in full to Microsoft. Critics say it gets round the 2022 national ban on hyperscale data centres because on paper it is three smaller data centres. According to NRC, it will use as much electricity in a year as the whole of Amsterdam.

Microsoft told NOS that it is aware of the demonstration. “We understand that this project stirs up strong emotions and respect people’s right to express their opinions peacefully. However, we do not condone actions that violate the law or endanger people’s safety.”

item.title: Cancelled Jewish exhibition back on table after mayor steps in
item.description:
Cancelled Jewish exhibition back on table after mayor steps in

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Amersfoort Mayor Lucas Bolsius has said he wants a cancelled Jewish exhibition at the Amsersfoort Museum to go ahead, and the museum has now agreed to look at how it can be staged. The museum announced earlier this week that it was cancelling the exhibition due to the situation in the Middle East and rising global tensions.

The exhibition, “300 Years Amersfoort Shul”, has been years in the making, and its last-minute cancellation has caused outrage in the Jewish community.

“Apparently, many struggle to distinguish between Jewish identity and Israel. The reflex to cancel performances in situations like this is becoming increasingly common across the cultural sector,” Alexander van Dijkhuizen, chairman of the Jewish Community of Amersfoort, is reported as saying in US Jewish newspaper The Algemeiner.

“It is essential not only to reflect on the past, but also to acknowledge the difficult circumstances facing the Jewish community today.”

Hard to manage

When museum director Paul Baltus cancelled the exhibition, he said possible reactions to it were hard to manage.

“As a small and vulnerable organisation, I do not want to expose my staff to that kind of pressure,” he told the AD. “While security guards can be hired and cameras installed, the reality is that our volunteers would still have to deal with a range of possible reactions.”

But the mayor said he wasn’t informed about that decision, and he met with the museum and Amersfoort’s Jewish community on Thursday to discuss how the exhibition can go ahead.

“I am enormously saddened,” the mayor told the city council on Wednesday. “Jewish history and present-day life belong to our city. That must get the attention it deserves.” He said it was painful that the community was being made to feel it is not permitted to exist.

After Thursday’s meeting, the city said in a statement that the city, the museum and the Jewish community would look together at how 300 years of Jewish life in Amersfoort could be shown in an exhibition. “It was a good and intensive conversation,” Bolsius said. “We jointly concluded that we consider it important that there is an exhibition telling the story of 300 years of Jewish culture in Amersfoort.”

The Amersfoort Synagogue dates back to 1727 and is the oldest functioning Ashkenazi synagogue in Western Europe. The Jewish community has planned a wide-ranging programme of concerts and performances to mark the synagogue’s 300th anniversary.

Earlier this week, a Jewish student association lecture at Maastricht University was cancelled less than an hour before it was due to start, with the university saying it couldn’t guarantee participants’ safety.

item.title: Skaters get three hours on natural ice as first frost arrives
item.description:
Skaters get three hours on natural ice as first frost arrives

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The first frost has appeared after temperatures dropped below freezing overnight in parts of the Netherlands, in Brabant, Limburg and parts of Zeeland, according to the national weather service KNMI.

It also allowed the season’s first natural ice skating in Gelderland for a couple of hours in early morning.

The lowest temperature was recorded in Woensdrecht in Brabant, at minus 1.2°. Ell in Limburg reached minus 1.1° and Westdorpe in Zeeland minus 0.4°.

It does not yet count as an official frost day though. For that, the temperature at the KNMI’s base in De Bilt, near Utrecht, has to fall below zero. Overnight it stayed at 0.8° there.

In Winterswijk, in Gelderland, the local skating club opened the country’s first natural ice rink of the season, even though there was only ground frost there. The club uses special techniques to make ice quickly.

“When you tell people that, they say ‘it can’t be done’. But it can,” chairman Auke Spijkstra told broadcaster NOS. “It’s wonderful to see all those enthusiastic people.” About 20 skaters took to the ice. The sun soon melted it, and the rink closed again at around 10am.

item.title: Verwey-Jonker Institute facing bankruptcy amid AI rise
item.description:
Verwey-Jonker Institute facing bankruptcy amid AI rise

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Verwey-Jonker Institute, an independent research institute in Utrecht, appears to be on the brink of bankruptcy, citing budget cuts and the rise of AI as the culprits. The Institute has applied to court for a suspension of payments.

Moving to a less expensive location and downsizing its board hasn’t been enough to save the beleaguered Institute. Broadcaster NOS also reported there’s been unrest within the agency’s leadership.

The Verwey-Jonker Institute, founded in 1993, addresses societal issues, providing research to governments, municipalities and others with “social value and impact”, according to its website. They work on issues such as poverty, youth, education, discrimination and domestic violence, among others.

The Institute says technological developments mean many of their clients are now using AI instead of engaging researchers.

While they say they want to continue their work, it will now be up to an administrator to see just how they can do that.

item.title: Graffiti group posts video of attack on Amsterdam metro
item.description:
Graffiti group posts video of attack on Amsterdam metro

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A group of some 20 masked and hooded graffiti writers stopped a metro in Amsterdam Nieuw-West and sprayed the entire train with paint within minutes, leaving passengers inside stranded.

The action took place at the Henk Sneevlietweg stop last Saturday on Halloween. A video uploaded Tuesday on YouTube by the anonymous graffiti writers’ group Locos Worldwide, titled “Amsterdam Nightmare”, shows the sprayers entering the station and speed-spraying the train in orange, purple and black before running away cheering.

They also threw a bicycle onto the tracks and spray painted the driver’s window, leaving the train unable to move.

Shaken and shocked

“Our driver is quite shocked by the incident,” a spokesman for Amsterdam transport company GVB said. “We can also imagine that this was a frightening situation for travellers.”

The GVB, which called the incident a “serious form of vandalism”, has filed a police report. It’s still not known who is responsible for the action, but the GVB says it plans to seek compensation from the “perpetrators” when they are identified.

They tagged the train with apparent acronyms ‘NSPSKU’ and ‘LCSNTC’. NSPS has been tagged on transit vehicles in the past.

Police say they are taking the incident “seriously” and have appealed to the public to come forward with any video images they may have.

The GVB says that while graffiti does happen, the scale of the Halloween night action is extraordinary. Not only was the driver severely shaken, but the ordeal was a “potentially terrifying situation for passengers as well”.

And, according to the GVB, it put them at risk. “There was not only a subway smeared, but also a bicycle thrown on the track. That entails major security risks,” a spokesman said.

Five years ago, Locos Worldwide uploaded another video showing a masked group spray painting an in-service Amsterdam metro. The group also posts similar actions that have taken place across Europe, including in Paris, Madrid and Copenhagen.

item.title: Five of seven Dutch reptile species in decline, CBS says
item.description:
Five of seven Dutch reptile species in decline, CBS says

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Five of the seven reptile species found in the Netherlands have declined over the past 12 years, according to new figures from national statistics office CBS and research foundation RAVON.

Only the wall lizard has grown in number since 2014, while the slow worm has stayed stable. On average, reptile populations have fallen since 2014 and are now roughly back at their 1994 level.

The viviparous, the common lizard, has fared worst, with numbers down almost 75% since 1994. The smooth snake has fallen by more than 60% since 1997, and the adder and grass snake are also in decline.

CBS said climate change may be hitting species that prefer cooler, wetter conditions, such as the common lizard and the adder. Overgrown habitats and fewer insects to eat are also likely factors.

Wall lizard numbers, by contrast, have risen more than five-fold since 1995, helped by the warmer climate.

item.title: KLM flight stranded in Bucharest after bomb threat
item.description:
KLM flight stranded in Bucharest after bomb threat

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

A KLM flight from Amsterdam to Tel Aviv received a bomb threat on Thursday and was then unable to leave Bucharest because of a technical problem, the airline told news agency ANP.

Flight KL461 received a bomb threat at 7.30pm while in Bucharest, everyone on board got off, and the plane was inspected. Romania’s intelligence agency said the pilots asked for a pyrotechnic inspection of the aircraft.

The plane was cleared to continue to Tel Aviv on Friday morning, but a technical fault was found just before departure. The flight was cancelled and passengers were put up in hotels. KLM is looking for alternative flights for them.

The KLM flight was one of at least 27 passenger flights hit by hoax bomb threats on Thursday, in countries including France, Italy, Bulgaria, Spain, Denmark, Poland, Romania, Ireland, the UK and the Czech Republic, according to Reuters.

Some planes made unplanned landings, and fighter jets escorted or intercepted others.

The office of the French prime minister said fighter jets intercepted an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome and escorted it to an airbase near Paris, after the pilot did not cooperate with the authorities as expected.

Spanish police received three emailed threats within 20 minutes, covering six Air Europa and Iberia flights.

It was the second wave this week. On Tuesday, at least seven passenger flights were targeted, and aircraft were searched in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy. No explosives were reported found.

The national counterterrorism agency NCTV says it does not know where the threats are coming from. “The number of bomb threats in such quick succession is striking and has the NCTV’s special attention,” a spokesperson told ANP. “Unfortunately, it is impossible to stop reports like this being made.”

item.title: Ajax, NEC and Twente win in Europe as AZ lose to Juventus
item.description:
Ajax, NEC and Twente win in Europe as AZ lose to Juventus

November 6, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Three of the four Dutch clubs playing in Europe on Thursday night won. Only AZ Alkmaar lost its match.

AZ lost 2-1 at home to Juventus in the Europa League.

NEC Nijmegen beat Omonia Nicosia 3-1, also in the Europa League. The Cypriot champions scored first, but NEC scored twice to make their first home win since August.

In the Conference League, Ajax thrashed Midtjylland 6-1 in Denmark.

FC Twente beat Pafos FC 3-1 in Enschede. They have now won all three of their games in the competition.
